documents.body: Patient: I got my first covid shot Wednesday at the community clinic in town (Moderna). They said to tell you. Second one is booked for Feb 24. Do I keep taking the methotrexate around it?

documents.body: Thanks, Janet, it's in your record now. Rheumatology groups have been suggesting holding the methotrexate for the one week after each dose if your RA is quiet - check with your rheumatologist, but that's reasonable. Keep the prednisone as is.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia
conditions.note: Poorly controlled; postprandial hyperglycemia with near-normal fasting values

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DIABETES FOLLOW-UP

58 next week. Says she's been following her meal plan and walking most days, but for a couple of months she has felt worn out and notices she is thirsty, mostly in the hour or two after eating. Weight has not changed. No increased urination, not up at night to void. No blurred vision, no lows.
Meds: metformin 1000 bid, glargine 20 u qhs; amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25; MTX 15 weekly, folic acid, prednisone 5; ferrous sulfate.

Vitals: BP 132/86, HR 78, BMI 29.
Exam: unremarkable - alert, no distress, mucous membranes moist, heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft, no edema, feet intact.

Labs (resulted this afternoon): fasting glucose 98. A1c 8.5. Two-hour glucose after a standard breakfast 220.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes, poorly controlled, now about 10 years. Fasting number is fine on the glargine; the problem is after meals - fits the thirst and fatigue. Updating the problem list to reflect hyperglycemia. Reviewed carbohydrate portions at breakfast and lunch, and to check a 2-hour reading after her largest meal a few times a week and send me the log.
2. HTN at goal.
3. PCV20 given today.
F/u 3 months.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: ankles swelling.
Noticed since early January, both legs, socks leave deep marks by evening; down a lot by morning. No chest pain, no orthopnea, no PND, no dyspnea on stairs beyond her baseline. No calf pain. No recent travel. No new meds.
Post-meal sugar log brought: mostly 190-240.
Exam: Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur, no JVD. Bilateral pitting edema to the lower shin, symmetric, nontender. Calves soft.
A/P:
1. Bilateral leg edema - differential includes amlodipine effect, venous, cardiac, renal. She has a strong family history of heart disease and smokes; she'd like a cardiologist to look at it. Referral placed. Leg elevation in the evening meanwhile.
2. T2DM - log reviewed, still high after meals; she wants to keep working on portions before adding anything.
Will see her after cardiology.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 03/09/2022
Reason: leg swelling.

Thank you for referring Ms. Krause, 58, about three months after her last diabetes visit with you. For two months both legs have been getting progressively puffier, worst toward evening and a bit better after a night with her feet up. She has had no chest pain, no breathlessness and no long trips.

History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes (poorly controlled), rheumatoid arthritis, iron deficiency anemia, osteopenia from long-term steroids. Medications: amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metformin, insulin glargine, methotrexate, prednisone, ferrous sulfate, folic acid. Allergies: NKDA. Family: father with CAD and MI at 68; mother diabetes, hypertension, stroke at 72. Smokes one pack daily, 30 pack-years.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 78, RR 16. 2+ pitting edema to the mid-shin on both sides. Remainder of the cardiovascular and general exam unremarkable.

Labs today: sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.0, BUN 14, albumin 4.5. Urinalysis without protein or blood.

Impression: Dependent bilateral edema from the calcium channel blocker. Normal renal function and albumin with no proteinuria argue against a renal or hepatic cause, and there are no features of heart failure.

Recommendations: Elevate the legs when seated. The amlodipine is the likely cause; whether to lower or replace it I will leave to you, as her pressure is above goal today. No cardiology follow-up needed unless new symptoms.

documents.title: Telephone Encounter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: PCP call. Reviewed cardiology letter with her: swelling put down to amlodipine; heart, kidney labs fine. Her BP was 142/88 there and she'd prefer not to juggle pills right now. Agreed to keep amlodipine 10 mg as is, elevate legs, revisit at next visit. She's relieved it isn't her heart.

orders.reason: Persistent eczematous change of the right nipple-areolar complex

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: rash on R nipple.
Has had an itchy, scaly patch on the right nipple since about June, at first small and red, now covering more of the nipple, sometimes crusting. She's been putting moisturizer on it. No lump felt, no discharge. Embarrassed to bring it up sooner.
Exam (chaperone present): Right nipple and part of areola red and scaly with some excoriation. No palpable mass either breast. No axillary adenopathy. Left breast normal.
A/P: Unilateral nipple dermatitis present ~5 months that has not settled - needs Paget disease excluded. Referred to breast surgery for evaluation with imaging and biopsy; marked urgent. Explained why I'm not just treating it as eczema. Her aunt had breast cancer, which she brought up.

documents.title: Breast Surgery Consultation
documents.author: breast surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE BREAST SURGERY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/05/2022

Ms. Krause is a 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes that has been hard to control and rheumatoid arthritis on long-term prednisone. For half a year she has had an itchy scaly eruption on the right nipple and areola. It started as a small red flaky spot, has gradually spread, and now and then oozes clear fluid. No nipple discharge and she has felt no lump.

Medications: amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, insulin glargine, methotrexate, prednisone 5 mg, ferrous sulfate, folic acid. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with invasive ductal breast cancer at 62.
Social: 30 pack-years, still smoking.

Exam: Right nipple-areolar complex erythematous with excoriations and a small area of ulceration. No mass in either breast. No palpable axillary adenopathy.

Imaging: diagnostic mammogram today shows a subtle area of increased density on the right without a discrete mass or calcifications.

Procedure: 4 mm punch biopsy of the right nipple skin under local anesthesia, tolerated well.

Impression: Unilateral nipple dermatitis concerning for Paget disease. Will call her with pathology and plan.

reports.text: Specimen: skin, right nipple, punch biopsy. Epidermis infiltrated by single and clustered large cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli. Immunostains: tumor cells CK7 positive.

documents.title: Results Routed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pathology from the breast surgeon's office received by fax and routed to PCP. Breast surgery will be calling the patient directly with the plan.

documents.body: I'm sorry, Janet - I saw the report this morning. Yes, front desk will put you in on the 20th for the pre-op visit. Bring your sugar log. You can message me any questions before then.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 74. PR, QRS and QT intervals normal. Normal axis. No ST or T wave abnormality.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OPERATIVE EVALUATION
Planned: right breast surgery (central lumpectomy) in January for biopsy-proven Paget disease of the nipple.
Functional capacity >4 METs (climbs 2 flights, carries groceries). No chest pain, syncope, dyspnea. No prior anesthesia problems (C-section, colonoscopies). No bleeding history.
Exam: Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Airway unremarkable. 1+ ankle edema (known, amlodipine).
ECG: NSR, normal.
Labs today: BMP, CBC, A1c.
Assessment: Low-risk breast procedure; RCRI 1 (insulin). No further cardiac testing.
Recommendations to surgeon:
- Metformin: hold the morning of surgery.
- Glargine: take 80% (16 units) the night before.
- Prednisone: take the morning dose; she has been on it >10 years - anesthesia to consider stress dosing.
- Methotrexate: may continue at this dose for a minor procedure; defer to rheumatology/surgeon.
- Antihypertensives: take amlodipine; hold HCTZ the morning of surgery.
- Smoking cessation strongly advised for wound healing - she will try to cut down.
